Industry News: DDR6 memory modules to be almost half the size of DDR5 and almost double the max speed

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You may not be able to buy memory right now, but the good news for a hopeful future is there's potentially quicker and smaller RAM on the horizon.
  • According to JEDEC, DDR6 will bring with it higher bandwidth, higher capacities, better reliability, more energy efficiency, and different form factors (via VideoCardz).
  • Starting with bandwidth, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at a speed of 12.8 GT/s and are set to move up to "14.4 GT/s and beyond." DDR5 maxes out at 9.2 GT/s, representing a sizable bump.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You may not be able to buy memory right now, but the good news for a hopeful future is there's potentially quicker and smaller RAM on the horizon. JEDEC, the council that sets industry standards for RAM, has published a preview of what DDR6 could look like, and it seems like it will be itty and bitty.

According to JEDEC, DDR6 will bring with it higher bandwidth, higher capacities, better reliability, more energy efficiency, and different form factors (via VideoCardz).

Starting with bandwidth, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at a speed of 12.8 GT/s and are set to move up to "14.4 GT/s and beyond." DDR5 maxes out at 9.2 GT/s, representing a sizable bump. It also expands the data bus from 64 to 96 DQ, which no doubt contributes to the bandwidth increase.

It has been revealed that that is fast, though not two times faster like DDR5 versus DDR4. It is worth noting, however, that memory modules tend to get faster over their lifetime so we don't know where that might end up.

Recent findings suggest that the module for DDR6 is now 74 mm, which is almost half of the 133 mm for DDR5. This is supposedly "intended to help accommodate higher system memory density", with DDR6 supporting up to 128 GB DRAM die density (double that of DDR5).

There are other gains to be had with DDR6 too. JEDEC notes it targets an improved performance-per-watt over DDR5 "through a change to VSS-terminated IO and data-center-focused low power modes".

JEDEC says DDR6 can support a "breadth of form factors", including RDIMM, UDIMM, CAMM.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

It has been revealed that now for one thing you may not want to hear, but might have already suspected: JEDEC states DDR6 is 'built for the data center". It says its interface is "optimised for high-capacity modules with configurations oriented to general purpose compute as well as AI inferencing and agentic AI, which demand more capacity and performance close to the CPU.".

Being built for data center usage does not mean consumers will be left out in the cold, of course, but it does further signal just how much memory is being designed for future AI usage. And the memory crisis seems set to last at least through 2027, even if Acer's CEO reckons it's impossible for it to last until 2030. It is all heavily reliant on how much memory supply can be ramped up and how much memory demand comes from the AI boom, which is certainly a hard-to-predict industry.

Continuing the trend of news you don't want to hear, we don't know when DDR6 is supposed to be available to the public. It seems like the release window is between 2028 and 2029, but we don't have any more information than that. And that's before musing on whether we non-AI data center owners will ever be able to afford the module. Hopefully, the memory crisis will cool off in a couple of years, and DDR6 will actually be affordable for PC gamers, though whether it will be relevant for PC gaming is a whole other thing. But, to steal a line from The Shawshank Redemption, "Hope is a dangerous thing".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

It has been revealed that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony stated that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Recent findings suggest that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Industry observers note that sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

Sources indicate that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was unveiled back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a newly introduced name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s.
  • Recent findings suggest that I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer.
  • Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a upcoming brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

Recent findings suggest that I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his blueprint.

Industry observers note that as for the latest playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

It has been revealed that fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

It has been revealed that marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that nicolas Cage and Christian Bale may seem like two very different kinds of actors, but they do have something in common.
  • Russell’s Madden – one of the buzzy titles on the 2026 movie schedule – chronicles the life and career of the titular football coach-turned-commentator.
  • I met Christian for the first time, decked out as Al.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nicolas Cage and Christian Bale may seem like two very different kinds of actors, but they do have something in common. They both truly commit to their roles no matter how bonkers or over-the-top they are. Bale and Cage have played characters who’ve gone bananas on screen, and that’s also the case with their latest movie, Madden. In the sports biopic, Cage and Bale play John Madden and Al Davis, respectively and wear a lot of prosthetics for the roles. And, as CinemaBlend learned, that’s surprisingly how their co-stars met them.

David O. Russell’s Madden – one of the buzzy titles on the 2026 movie schedule – chronicles the life and career of the titular football coach-turned-commentator. Cage really got into the role, and his physical transformation alone is proof of that. The same can be remarked for Bale, who’s known to transform by gaining or losing weight. So what’s it like to actually see the pair on set and in their element? Well, I recently spoke to co-stars Sienna Miller and Kathryn Hahn about that, and Miller shared a funny story about meeting Bale as Al:.

I met Christian for the first time, decked out as Al. He came to say hi, which was very very exciting, and he was like, you know, [mimics Al Davis’ voice] ‘We're gonna have fun doing this,’ you know? And he's all in the voice, and I was beside myself, because I think he's really the GOAT, but then he's very funny on set and loves to play. And I'd imagined a real intensity, and there is once he's performing. But he loves to have a laugh off, you know, in between, and was not as you know — I think as actors, we're like a bunch of kids in a fancy dress cupboard, and that's what it felt like on this.

Miller plays the role of Carol Sagal Davis – the wife of late Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis – so she and Bale spent quite a bit of time together on set. For me, the mere thought of meeting Bale when he’s not in character seems intimidating, so I can’t even fathom the idea of being introduced to him while he’s decked out in prosthetics. What also has me chuckling is the thought of the Oscar winner keeping his character’s distinct accent while introducing himself to Miller. Nevertheless, it sounds like the two got along just fine.

Sources indicate that during my recent interview, of course, I was also shocked to hear about Kathryn Hahn – who plays Virginia Fields Madden – meeting Nic Cage for the first time on set while he was under all of that heavy makeup. And, believe it or not, at the time we spoke, Hahn mentioned she had never even been in Cage’s presence when he wasn’t in costume and prosthetics. She explained:.

In a recent development, we were just saying that I've never seen Nic not as John Madden, so it's going to be so weird to finally be like, ‘Nice to meet you.’.... It's not like he was like a method actor, but there was a way of being that he instantly just filled out whenever he would put those prosthetics on. So yeah, that was the first time I met him was as John Madden, basically.

Something I can’t help but wonder is whether Cage’s Longlegs co-stars ever met him when he wasn’t dressed as the titular serial killer. I can’t imagine Cage sparking unease on set whenever he wasn’t giving that creepy and perfect performance. Yet I can definitely admit I’d still be genuinely creeped out just by being in his presence.

Industry observers note that but, as for Madden, I can imagine those on-set interactions being memories that neither Hahn nor Miller will ever forget. Speaking of these two talented actresses, they also wear prosthetics at different points in the movie, though they arguably aren’t as extensive as those of their on-screen partners. Still, like Cage and Bale, Miller and Hahn fully commit to their roles as well, delivering some humorous performances in the process.

Now, if anything I just want to know what it was like when Kathryn Hahn and Nicolas Cage finally met at the Madden premiere. I’m tempted to assume that was a fun moment. But, that aside, check out the movie, which is playing in select theaters and streaming with a Prime Video subscription.

In a recent development, right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was confirmed in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

📅 10 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • Sources indicate that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • Sources indicate that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Sources indicate that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

Sources indicate that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja remarked it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

It has been revealed that the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

It has been revealed that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

In a recent development, there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#5248. Industry News: 7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1218 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: 7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way.
  • Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases.
  • When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way. While modern titles keep several staples of the genre, such as a fixed story, a focus on character development, innovation in the battle system, and some wacky progression systems, sometimes it feels like they leave behind certain mechanics that could be put to great use today. Many JRPGs of yesteryear featured unique mechanics that were either never re-explored, or, if they were, remained confined to indie games and flew under the radar of many players.

Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases. Most are battle-related, though a few, if properly implemented, could expand exploration and even improve how the game's systems interact. That is not to say they have never appeared in other games throughout the years, but I would love to see them become much more mainstream.

When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing. When chaining attacks, you can aim at enemies' limbs, yet all I ever did was try to go straight for the head or body to defeat the foe as fast as possible. How naive I was, because against bosses, that mindless strategy never paid off, especially if I was not wielding an appropriate weapon.

Recent findings suggest that this mechanic of targeting different body parts has popped up in other JRPGs, though usually you can only hit distinct areas when an enemy is preparing a specific attack. I would love to see a JRPG reuse this mechanic exhaustively, letting players willingly target different enemy limbs and trigger distinct tactical outcomes.

One of Star Ocean's greatest strengths is its Item Creation system. To me, gaining levels wasn't about learning newly introduced combat skills, but it was all about earning points to invest in Customization and unlock new crafting potential, whether forging an endgame weapon at the start of the game or diving into other side activities. Still, the most entertaining feature, even at the cost of my relationship with my party members, was Pickpocketing.

According to recent reports, leveling up your Pickpocketing skill lets you steal from every NPC in town and score the wildest variety of items. The sheer thrill of not knowing what you would get, whether a simple consumable or an insanely overpowered piece of gear, was endlessly fun and had me making the rounds through town as if I were living inside GTA. As mentioned, doing so affects how your party members perceive the protagonist, so if you are aiming for a specific ending, watch out for the consequences of your actions.

According to recent reports, this entry is less about battle mechanics and more about dungeon delving. As much as I love modern JRPGs, especially for their evolution in combat gameplay, narrative, and character development, I feel some are still a bit lacking in the level design department. Too many dungeons are simply streamlined corridors, featuring an occasional puzzle that solves itself before you even begin thinking through the solution.

In a recent development, plenty of classic JRPGs boasted incredible level design, but if I had to highlight just one, it would be Wild Arms. This series blended the interactive tools of action-adventure games and let the scope of exploration expand incrementally. Moreover, acquiring latest tools encouraged backtracking and re-exploring older dungeons, much like a Metroidvania, to hunt down hidden treasures.

I never had much contact with Sega consoles growing up, which led me to neglect their JRPG catalog for quite a while. I played Phantasy Star IV fairly recently, and during my playthrough, a friend told me to set up Macros using specific skills while emphasizing that the execution order mattered. So I complied, and when I stepped into battle, oh boy, what a beautiful surprise.

For those who don't know, depending on the sequence in which you cast spells and skills, they fuse together to unleash an entirely fresh combo attack. It is a deeply entertaining combo system that later surfaced in future JRPGs like Breath of Fire IV. It feels distinct from two characters simply chaining standard turns together, because there is a real sense of mystique in discovering the combinations, and I will confess that without a GameFAQs guide, I never would have figured them all out. Still, it is pretty amazing and elevated turn-based combat to new heights.

Industry observers note that staying on the topic of skill combos, Chrono Trigger pulled off something similar yet distinctly its own. If two or three party members mastered specific techniques and had their ATB gauges filled simultaneously, they could execute a Double or Triple Tech, each carrying a unique effect. The very first time I discovered this, as I imagine most players did, was with Crono and Lucca's Fire Whirl. A whole upcoming world of tactical possibilities opened up in that exact moment.

Industry observers note that chrono Trigger pushed the concept even further, and just when I expected the game to stick to Double Techs, the JRPG introduced Triple Techs. I don't know about you, but I built my entire party around these Techs, and luckily, nearly every character paired well with the rest of the roster. Triple Techs were slightly more restrictive, yet they still allowed for remarkably efficient setups, especially when hunting for Techs capable of healing the entire party at once.

In a recent development, breath of Fire is my favorite JRPG series, and within it, Breath of Fire III stands as my absolute favorite entry. Whenever people ask me why, a massive part of my reasoning rests on its Gene splicing system, a feature Breath of Fire IV dropped for reasons I still don't understand, which was a real shame. I loved transforming into dozens of distinct dragons, even if Ryu and Fou-Lu's half-dragon forms looked awesome in their own right.

Essentially, you discovered Dragon Genes scattered across the world and could combine up to three at once to transform Ryu into wildly different dragon forms, each boasting unique strengths and abilities. The thing is, I don't necessarily need the exact Gene system back, but I would love a transformation-focused JRPG where characters can shift forms mid-battle and completely alter the flow of combat. Even better if those transformations feature distinct variations that actively reward exploration.

In a recent development, I know there are many, many caveats surrounding the progression mechanics of Final Fantasy VIII, though I feel the bulk of player complaints stems from the Draw system rather than the Junction system itself. There is a historical reason behind that, as Hiroyuki Ito, creator of both the ATB and Junction systems, left the Final Fantasy VIII team before finalizing the battle mechanics to direct Final Fantasy IX, leaving his original vision somewhat incomplete.

According to recent reports, just imagine what it could have been if fully realized. The Junction system is remarkably dynamic. Beyond simply slotting spells to boost each character's raw stats, you could attach status ailments to basic physical attacks, build elemental resistances, tailor one character toward magic and agility while turning another into a pure strength powerhouse, and so on. Pair that flexibility with specialized commands learned through Guardian Forces, and what appears on the surface to be standard turn-based combat suddenly gains deep strategic layers.

  • Shenmue made headlines back in 1999 as the most expensive game ever made, with a reported $70 million budget – that'd be about $140 million, accounting for inflation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is finally here, and some players have been surprised to find themselves spending more time running errands and doing home repair than, you know, stealing cars through the game's opening hours. Rockstar was absolutely devoted to spending that vast development budget simulating the minutiae of Jason and Lucia's lives, and it's all pretty reminiscent of another infamously expensive game: Sega's Shenmue.

Shenmue made headlines back in 1999 as the most expensive game ever made, with a reported $70 million budget – that'd be about $140 million, accounting for inflation. That number has, of course, been eclipsed multiple times over through the past few decades, but it's still pretty expensive, especially in a world where AAA-beating GOTY contenders like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 are being made for less than $10 million.

Recent findings suggest that we still don't know Rockstar's actual budget for GTA 6, but it's tough to imagine it's anything less than the upcoming most expensive game ever made. There is, of course, a key difference between Grand Theft Auto and Shenmue: Sega's game was not financially successful, failing to recoup its development costs.

Yet Shenmue developed a cult following thanks to its obvious ambition. It was promoted as the first part of a multi-game martial arts epic, which would see protagonist Ryo Hazuki on a globe-trotting quest for revenge. But fighting makes up only a tiny part of the game. You instead spend much of your time exploring a small but densely packed open world, living out Ryo's day-to-day life as you rummage through drawers, drive forklifts, and question wandering NPCs for clues to your next objective.

Sources indicate that the early hours of GTA 6 offer a lot more possibility for high-octane chaos, but the game gently encourages you to instead spend your time restoring your home, running errands for neighbors, working out, eating meals, and chatting up random NPCs. In a way, it feels like the fulfillment of Shenmue's ambition – the life simulation now offers genuine payoffs instead of the charming jank we got in 1999.

You'll find this sort of comparison coming up again and again among retro gaming sickos on social media. "Gta 6 is not for the 'normals'," Twitter user drag writes. ""it's for real gamers who spent hours on shenmue buying toy capsules of sonic, it's 89.99 deadly premonition.".

"Played a couple hours into GTA6 and um… Yeah, it's a Shenmue game," Alex Lemley indicates on Bluesky. "They made a Shenmue game, actually. It's a really good Shenmue game, but it's Shenmue.".

The examples just don't stop, but maybe gum puts it best in this tweet: "they're calling it the shenmue of 2026.".

#5246. Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1073 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Industry observers note that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • It has been revealed that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Industry observers note that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

It has been revealed that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

According to recent reports, just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

It has been revealed that as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Recent findings suggest that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell states. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

Relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent enhancement is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell claims foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly.".

It has been revealed that I ask if it was always the blueprint to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell notes spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a significant part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Sims 4 will soon get a latest upgrade to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it intends to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Sources indicate that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with fresh and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Recent findings suggest that pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in fresh saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

According to recent reports, you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a game that's essentially all collectibles, Dice Hoarder has an extra set that can be tough to find.

  • Luckily, none of these dice are hidden amid the sea of dice all over the floor, so you don't have to worry about sifting through them all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a game that's essentially all collectibles, Dice Hoarder has an extra set that can be tough to find. Ten "edible" dice are hidden throughout the store, and you eat them when you find them, so realistically, you're just collecting them in your stomach.

That said, even though they aren't hidden among the rest of the dice around the shop, some aren't too bad, and others are exceptionally hard to spot. Don't be fooled, either; the cheese dice might look edible, but they fall into the Special category. Nope, instead, this is where you can find the edible dice in Dice Hoarder.

Luckily, none of these dice are hidden amid the sea of dice all over the floor, so you don't have to worry about sifting through them all. They'll be mostly on shelves and stuck in odd places where you wouldn't think to look for regular stock.

The edible dice set you get after sorting the whole store doesn't count toward the collectible count.

If you do come across them, though, there's no way to confuse them with the standard dice. We're going to number these for the sake of a list, but you can collect them in any order you find them.

Edible Die #1 is hidden just behind the pillow on the bed in the office. It's not too hard to spot, but if you're not looking for it, you might miss it.

Edible Die #2 is hidden on the desk in the office, just behind the cup and saucer.

Edible Die #3 is hidden on the shelf just outside the office, behind the potted plant. The color helps it blend in a bit with the shelf, but from the right angle you can spot it.

It has been revealed that edible Die #4 is hidden behind the plant pot in the corner of the store next to the window directly across from the office. It's good to have the Nimble Step ability so you can crouch and find this one.

Edible Die #5 is hidden behind a small potted plant on the windowsill just to the left of Hidden Die #4.

Recent findings suggest that edible Die #6 is hidden under the standing lamp's lampshade. You'll need to have Nimble Step to grab this one because you can't see underneath without crouching.

Edible Die #7 is hidden on top of the curtain rod in the corner to the left of the standing lamp. Even if you know where it is, it's hard to spot, so move your mouse cursor around the spot for a while until it highlights.

According to recent reports, edible Die #8 is hidden on the main counter, behind the stack of books on the right. It's closest to the clear resin dice and stands out because of its bright color.

Edible Die #9 is hidden on the shelf behind the main counter, on the thick, green book.

Edible Die #10 is hidden under the main counter, behind the two stacked trunks in the shadows.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one of the first things GTA 6 players searched for was strip club locations—genuinely, data doesn't lie. So, as a responsible guide writer, I loaded up the game and proceeded to spend my initial hours beelining around Leonida's hotspots. There are a few different strip clubs in Leonida, each with their own price range and different activities to try (that sounds sordid, but I'm also talking about, like, pool tables).

There are three strip clubs in the game I've found, plus a load of other night spots, like the Rusty Anchor close to where Jason starts, that have drinking and other activities, too.

According to recent reports, this fancy strip club in downtown Vice City is the classiest option you have available, but also the priciest. It's quite easy to get here, even from Leonida Keys where Jason starts—just drive along route 1 towards Hamlet, merge onto route 97, and head north into Downtown. The clubs are just to the right of the giant crossroads route interchange in west Vice City. NINE1NINE itself is next door to The Vault club. This is the best option if you have a lot of money to burn, but also it feels a bit too fancy.

According to recent reports, if you want a private dance, same as with previous GTA games, you just need to greet the dancer in question and then use the interaction icon to pay for it. Since this club is fancier, you can also get a private dance by interacting with the person by the entrance to the private rooms.

I appreciated NINE1NINE's lively club atmosphere, but I also ran out of cash very fast. Maybe one to try later in the game when you're a lot richer.

Recent findings suggest that this strip club in Vice City's Crosstown is directly north from NINE1NINE, but there's a catch: this place only unlocks via the main story. I assume it's Chapter 3, considering that's when you meet its owner, but either way, it'll be a while before you can visit this establishment.

I assume in terms of price range, it's fancier than Delights (the cheapest option), but less fancy than NINE1NINE. This club gets one star because it wouldn't let me in, though maybe I'll change this review once I actually get inside.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that delights in Port Gellhorn is your cheapest option and it's a bit more rough and ready relative to NINE1NINE. It's also a long drive if you're just starting the game and want to visit the club in the northwest of the map. You'll want to drive to Hamlet via route 1 from the Keys, as with NINE1NINE, but then head northwest on route 82 towards Capri, then 103 merging onto the 404, past the airport towards Port Gellhorn. Bank a right when you reach the town, and the substantial Delights billboard to find it a little way further, on your left.

This club has stage dancing, unlike NINE1NINE, pool tables, but also cheaper private dances, tips, and drinks. Hilariously, some of the dancers also already know Jason and will actually make comments about him. I went here early in the game and one of the dancers mentioned Jason and Lucia, so I guess he must be a regular. In general, this club has a lot more character than the others, it's reasonably priced, also you can play pool—four stars. I also witnessed an old woman on a mobility scooter mugging someone outside, which gave added entertainment value.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

It has been revealed that you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

Recent findings suggest that I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Right now, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw rapidly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is debuted over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

Industry observers note that the screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

It has been revealed that I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

It has been revealed that the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Recent findings suggest that still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

It has been revealed that casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

In a recent development, I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

It has been revealed that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With a game as gorgeous as GTA 6, could you want even more, graphically?
  • In both cases, you can either use a capture card or Remote Play to get the game streamed to your gaming PC.
  • You just have to run a PowerShell command, get Remote Play linked up, and run a short setup with the new Veyra executable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With a game as gorgeous as GTA 6, could you want even more, graphically? Well, some PC gamers seem to be answering 'yes' and throwing some DLSS 5 neural rendering into the mix. Oh, and perhaps more importantly for those of you concerned about the low frame rate on console, they're managing to up the frame rate to 60 fps, too.

Sources indicate that how, you ask? In both cases, you can either use a capture card or Remote Play to get the game streamed to your gaming PC. Then, for DLSS 5, you use a tool called Veyra, which can be easily installed and set up by running it via another tool from the modder Phosphen (via VideoCardz).

You just have to run a PowerShell command, get Remote Play linked up, and run a short setup with the new Veyra executable. Assuming, that is, you have a graphics card that can handle the extra DLSS 5 work. And assuming you can get it to work—my colleague couldn't get the tool to link up to his PS5 when he tried.

Judging by some gameplay capture of GTA 6 with DLSS 5 running on top, and to perhaps state the obvious, it's very graphically impressive. That goes for both the environment and characters.

This tool should get you up and running at 60 fps, too, using frame gen. Essentially, whether by 60 fps capture card or via Remote Play, each of the game's 30 frames per second is duplicated, giving you a 60 fps output that still feels like 30 fps. The tool removes the duplicated frames and then adds frame gen to double them, giving you genuine upcoming frames interpolated between each actually rendered one. A proper 60 fps, but using frame gen.

It has been revealed that naturally, this will add some latency, especially because extra latency from frame gen is most noticeable when starting at a low base frame rate. Still, it might be worth a try.

Industry observers note that you also don't have to use that tool try to and hit 60 fps, as you could try Lossless Scaling instead. You have to pay for that on Steam, but it lets you add upscaling and frame gen to a bunch of different windows or games, not just GTA 6. If you use this method, you just wrap it over your Remote Play stream of GTA 6.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

One potential problem with this method, though, relates to what the modder indicates in their readme: "Frame generation fed with copies makes stutter instead of smoothness." So, if you use Lossless Scaling with GTA 6 streamed over Remote Play for frame gen, the already-doubled output frame rate—ie, the duplicated frames—will likely cause a problem for frame gen, causing stuttering. So, it might be best to stick to upscaling only when using this method.

GTA 6 is a gorgeous game even without DLSS 5, but it doesn't seem like too much hassle to try out the neural rendering, too, if you have the PC for it. And speaking to the frame rate, I imagine there might be more interest in getting this upped to 60 fps on its own, so the tool might be worth a look.

Recent findings suggest that 2. Best budget: GameSir Nova Lite.

Tech Report: A Guide To Contraband Smuggling In Probably Stolen

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With a name like Probably Stolen, it's no wonder that the underground world of stolen and illicit goods is alive and well in this cyberpunk shop sim game.
  • In a recent development, whether you're running guns, dealing drugs, or simply trading in stolen goods, there's a lot to consider when carrying contraband.
  • In a recent development, the Republic bans regular citizens from owning certain items, and definitely bans their sale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With a name like Probably Stolen, it's no wonder that the underground world of stolen and illicit goods is alive and well in this cyberpunk shop sim game.

In a recent development, whether you're running guns, dealing drugs, or simply trading in stolen goods, there's a lot to consider when carrying contraband. Here's what you need to know to avoid getting arrested...in the game, of course.

In a recent development, the Republic bans regular citizens from owning certain items, and definitely bans their sale. Because of this, Security regularly performs inspections looking for these banned items. When a Security Inspector comes to your shop looking for contraband, depending on the level of inspector you get, they'll check your inventory, back storage, counter, display case, and trash bin.

There are four levels of contraband in Probably Stolen: low, mid, high, and critical.

In a recent development, there are a few key upgrades and machines you really need to invest in if you're going to deal in contraband. Some have to do with producing product, while others will make it much easier to get away with carrying and selling it.

Recent findings suggest that if you opt to get the Gunsmith upgrade and any of its successors from Joe Wild's network, you gain legal access to a ton of firearms and ammunition, which can make selling them much easier. Yes, it's not technically contraband anymore once you get your permit, but it's still weaponry, and it sells to all the same people. Plus, this way, you don't have to worry about your criminal record when you sell lower-level guns. If you have a high enough reputation with them, you can even buy guns and ammo from Security.

If you're really dedicated to going to criminal route, though, you can invest in the Lower Levels Chemist upgrade, which lets you buy illegal drugs over the phone, or the Upper Level Pharmacist upgrade, which lets you buy legal medications over the phone. If you buff these with their Shareholder upgrades, you get access to a steady supply of Dream Dust and Oxymore. You might also get the Retired Chemist upgrade, which gives you a chemistry starting kit that lets you produce your own substances with the right recipes.

Sources indicate that you might also want to invest in the Criminal Networking upgrade, which boosts your reputation with the Black Market and sends either a criminal buyer, thief, or mercenary to your store the day after you pay the nightly fee of 45 credits. This'll help you move product promptly.

You need a smuggler's bay if you're going to trade contraband; having your stolen or illegal goods in a smuggler's bay is the only way to avoid detection during an inspection. Without one, you'll always get caught by Security, which makes your life a lot harder than it needs to be. Get one from Dr. Jackson as promptly as you can. If you start with the Fence scenario, you get one automatically.

Smuggler's bays have a five by five grid of cells to store things in, and can be expanded with the Underground Exchange to have an eight by eight grid; to expand it, you'll need to leave a regular smuggler's bay and eight Oxymore injectors in the trash can overnight.

In a recent development, if you're planning to grow any of your own substances, especially Nightmare Caps, you'll need a Hydroponic Smuggling Module. A Hydroponic Smuggling Module gets rid of the contraband label on anything growing in a hydroponic system, which protects your Nightmare Caps from detection during inspections while they're growing. Of course, to grow Nightmare Caps, you'll need the Nightmare Module as well, so make sure you organize your module bay to have enough room for both.

If you're dealing in firearms, you're going to need a Gunsmith Storage Bay. This is a particularly major storage bay — a 17 x 10 grid — that holds all of your firearms, firearms parts, ammo, and gun mods. You can also store things like 3D printing filament, screwdrivers, tasers, and stun guns in it to free up space in your regular storage.

Inevitably, if you're constantly buying and selling stolen goods — even if you're letting the heat die down before you sell them — you're going to end up with marks building up on your record, which can get you arrested if you're not careful. Thankfully, there are a few things you can get to mitigate this problem, all of which can be purchased through Joe Wild's network.

Sources indicate that you get a copy of your criminal record from The Mentor during the tutorial. If you check it, you can see how suspicious Security is of you, whether there are any active investigations, and if so, for what crimes. Use this information and all of these upgrades in combination to balance your criminal activity and you'll be golden.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old.
  • "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding upcoming content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 revision.
  • According to recent reports, "The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 patch to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are latest quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

"You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding upcoming content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 revision. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

According to recent reports, "The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

In a recent development, as laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several newly introduced dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

In a recent development, more clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A latest opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

It has been revealed that "All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

You can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a fresh playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

Breaking: Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has confirmed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Recent findings suggest that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has confirmed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Recent findings suggest that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Industry observers note that once downloaded, you’ll find a fresh Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

According to recent reports, all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

Recent findings suggest that the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

In a recent development, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big newly introduced update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.
