The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

It has been revealed that that version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

According to recent reports, forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, right now occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

Industry observers note that at the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Sources indicate that steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Industry observers note that game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

It has been revealed that forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer.
  • It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 certainly does that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 (well, some of us) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

In a recent development, GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

According to recent reports, I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?

I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

Industry observers note that the second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.

According to recent reports, I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 rapidly ceased to be an glitch, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it launched on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version presently available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

Sources indicate that it's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the massive screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

It has been revealed that truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.

According to recent reports, low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers. Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever indicates that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

Industry observers note that of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.

Recent findings suggest that is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.

I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob stated, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

I think it being consistent is key.

It has been revealed that but that's really infrequent. I think it being consistent is key. I'm on a PS5 Slim, by the way, not a Pro. That's not to say I still can't wait to see it at higher frame rates when it finally gets to PC. But 30 fps feels mostly fine for the time being.

It has been revealed that it was actually spending a lot of time playing with handheld gaming PCs and laptops with integrated graphics that reminded me I shouldn't give as much of a shit about frame rate as I do. Largely that obsession is born of having high-end hardware sat in my desktop PC, but when crashing around with a range of handhelds I'm reminded of the old days when 30 fps was a target for PC games, too.

It's also reminded me that it really depends on the game engine, as well. Not every 30 fps game looks the same as other 30 fps games. And Rockstar has obviously worked incredibly hard to make sure that 30 fps looks as good as it possible can. Otherwise why would that be a solid target for all four of the console platforms it's released on?

For the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth.

It has been revealed that I've been playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X, which does suffer from the odd dip in frame rate, too—though oddly I've only really noticed it during canned animations the characters do starting certain actions, such as opening the trunk of a car or pulling something out of it. But for the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth. And not just by using motion blur. For the record, I'm running that at 0 and have not looked back.

I'm less happy about the vignetting that I'm getting around the darkened edges of the screen, but I'm playing it blown up on a 4K projector so I've got plenty of screen real estate to enjoy. And I have been, thoroughly enjoying it, I mean. The frame rate, for me, hasn't got in the way once.

Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three substantial updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

In a recent development, coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This enhancement will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

It has been revealed that late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major patch. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April upgrade will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

It has been revealed that are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

Contrary to what Marvel fans may think, Gambit star Channing Tatum says he hasn't toned down his mutant's accent in Avengers: Doomsday, it's just less Cajun French.

Sources indicate that "I think I have been quoted in the press as toning down the accent. That is not exactly what I'm doing. I'm just speaking less Cajun French," said Tatum to Associated Press. "It's hard to explain, but basically Cajun French is French that almost French people can't understand. So I'm speaking less of that, but the Cajun accent is still there.".

Tatum first took to the screen as Gambit in Deadpool and Wolverine, where he sported a rather thick accent. In Marvel comics, the hero, real name Remy LeBeau, does indeed speak with an Acadiana twang, reflecting his Louisiana heritage. However, fans were quick to point out the difference in Gambit's accent in the first listen at his voice ahead of Doomsday, which arrived earlier this month in a Dunkin Donuts commercial.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, Tatum reminds fans that Doomsday is a very different movie from Deadpool 3, which might explain his change in cadence. "The movie and the tone in general is not Deadpool tone. Shawn Levy and Ryan Reynolds have their own tone that is specific to the Deadpool movies," explained Tatum. "The Russos, they have comedy and levity in their movies, but they definitely will punch you in the gut emotionally as well. So I think you're going to get a lot more drama. There's going to be a lot of drama in the movie, let me just say that.".

Sources indicate that though he couldn't give too much away, Tatum said we can "expect a little more emotional moments" from his mutant. "The movie is going to take you on a ride. We get to see a little bit more of Gambit's fighting style," added the star. We have already seen Gambit flick some cards at Shang-Chi in the Doomsday trailer, but the hero will have to learn to work as a team if he wants to defeat Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom as he threatens to destroy multiple Marvel timelines.

Gambit will be joined by other X-Men in the Marvel Phase 6 movie, including Patrick Stewart's Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen's Magneto, James Marsden's Cyclops, Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler, and Rebecca Romijn's Mystique.

Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and shows on the way.

GTA 6 Base PS5 Performance Suffers 'Minor' and 'Sustained' Frame Rate Drops, But It's 'Unwavering' on PS5 Pro

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (442 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As you'd expect, it sounds like PS5 Pro is the absolute best place to play GTA 6 at launch — but what about playing it on Sony's standard console?
  • First things first, Digital Foundry can't stress enough just how technically impressive Rockstar's latest open world is.
  • Industry observers note that on PS5 Pro, that 30fps is supposed to be "unwavering".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you'd expect, it sounds like PS5 Pro is the absolute best place to play GTA 6 at launch — but what about playing it on Sony's standard console? Our pals over at Digital Foundry have been putting it to the test.

First things first, Digital Foundry can't stress enough just how technically impressive Rockstar's latest open world is. In terms of simulating a living and breathing environment, it's completely unmatched — and that's the main reason why it's capped at just 30 frames-per-second with no graphics options to choose from.

Industry observers note that on PS5 Pro, that 30fps is supposed to be "unwavering". The report describes performance as "exceptionally robust" with "perfect frame pacing" — meaning that the game feels super responsive despite its 30fps cap.

GTA 6 also benefits massively from the Pro's built-in PSSR upscaling tech, to the point where it "convincingly mimics native 4K" resolution. Compared to playing on the base PS5, the image clarity is noticeably sharper, especially when it comes to the smaller details (of which there are many).

But to be clear, it's not like GTA 6 is a mess on the base PS5 — it just comes with some drawbacks.

It has been revealed that alongside the aforementioned downgrade in visual clarity, the game struggles to maintain a solid 30fps at times. The frame rate holds up fine during general gameplay, but it looks like busier scenarios start to drag it down.

You can get "minor dips" when driving at speed, with more "sustained" drops occurring when you're partaking in especially hectic combat encounters, complete with explosions.

These bigger bouts of choppiness can reportedly see the frame rate drop down into the mid-20s, which is obviously far from unplayable, but it's certainly not ideal.

But again, Digital Foundry makes it clear that Rockstar had to compromise on overall performance to deliver on its ridiculously ambitious open world vision — which falls in line with what the developer told us here at Push Square.

It has been revealed that indeed, the analysis heaps praise on the game's borderline photorealistic lighting, and "arguably the best implementation of ray tracing we've seen to date". All in all, Digital Foundry's just blown away by the sheer level of detail that's on display at all times — which is also something that Sammy wrote about at length in his GTA 6 PS5 review.

But what do you make of this tech report? Are you playing GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, or PS5? Are you still disappointed by the 30fps cap? Feel free to wait for the inevitable PS6 version in the comments section below.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

Industry observers note that the Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

Industry observers note that while the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

It has been revealed that the benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Sources indicate that version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A newly introduced Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.

According to recent reports, the teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation. The former has been responsible for some of the most well-regarded entries in the Assassin's Creed series along with key entries in the Far Cry franchise.

The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.

GamesIndustry.biz states that the layoffs account for less than 4% of the total workforce at the studios, and that the employees affected were working on projects that had either been cancelled or significantly changed.

Here's the statement provided by Ubisoft:.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations. As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Ubisoft's next major release is Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 classic Rayman Legends, developed in collaboration by Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it. After mere hours in the game, I'm already coming to terms with the scale of it; not just the size of the map, but the attention to detail on every object and interaction. But I have to remind myself, this is sure to be the worst version of GTA 6 we'll ever play.

Sources indicate that that sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite. If this is where the game is at launch, at its most barebones, running on years-old consoles on their way out, then think of what it will be like at its peak.

I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're presently playing on consoles.

Recent findings suggest that A part of that is the possible frame rate bump from running on modern PC hardware. The standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X are powered by pretty outdated architectures by today's standards: RDNA 2 and Zen 2. You're looking at the Radeon RX 6000 series and Ryzen 3000 series for PC equivalents.

Sources indicate that these chips have recently received support for more modern ML-powered FSR upscaling techniques from AMD, though Rockstar has only seen fit to enable FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S to help the underpowered console along. Sony also has AMD-powered upscaling tech for the PS5 Pro, but the standard PS5 doesn't get a whiff of that.

Recent findings suggest that it's only really the PS5 Pro with a more modern GPU—loosely equivalent to an RX 7800 XT—that might temper expectations for how fast the game may run on a modern gaming PC. Rockstar has stated the PlayStation 5 Pro wouldn't be capable of a steady 60 fps even with the more powerful hardware compared to the base model; however, hints at the sluggish CPU as perhaps the weak link. The PS5 Pro runs the same old eight-core CPU as the standard PS5, and if Rockstar's engine can make use of faster, more multithreaded CPUs with lots of cache, we should see a performance bump on PC.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to exclude older gaming PCs. The Xbox Series S can cope with GTA 6, so should many gaming PCs of all levels. Notably so if Rockstar offers a range of upscaling options.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's ubiquitous upscaling that should make an even bigger difference to an eventual PC release and performance on all manner of PC. We know the game supports FSR 4.1, as both Sony and Microsoft are already using this as the foundation for their upscaling technologies on console, and Red Dead Redemption 2 offers both FSR and DLSS on PC. Since that game's release, we've seen the advent of frame generation technologies from both AMD and Nvidia, which could further increase how smooth GTA 6 feels on PC.

Recent findings suggest that as a serial settings tweaker, I've been sorely disappointed by the sliders, or lack thereof, available to me in GTA 6 on the base PS5. I want levels to this stuff; an advanced menu for advanced men like me. I want to manage the foliage detail, draw distance, and ray-traced effects. Speaking of which, I'm sure we'll have the option to enable ray-traced shadows, presently exclusive to the PS5 Pro, and crank up the quality of most effects in the game on PC.

In a recent development, the non-RT shadows are one of the few noticeable drawbacks about the standard PS5 version of GTA 6 I'm right now playing. They can pop in and out from reflections, and there is a jagginess to them in places.

Industry observers note that is any game going to be modded more than GTA 6? Our Joshua has been busy modding GTA 5 to try to turn it alchemy-like into GTA 6 for months now, and he never ran out of mods to install. While he may have strayed from his original mission almost immediately, the message is clear: GTA 6 is going to have a seriously busy mod scene.

The game will be all the better for it, too. Not every mod is going to enable a roving band of militant furries (Joshua's words, and no need to mod those into GTA 6) or trap the player in a tiny car; I'm sure GTA 6 will actually be a better game for the efforts of modders. It just takes a PC version and some intrepid people to make it happen.

This one is easy; one of the reasons for GTA 5's long-lasting legacy is the combination of GTA Online and custom jobs via the creator. Neither of which are actually here for GTA 6 yet. So on a very basic level, and you don't have to be a PC gamer to agree on this point, GTA 6 is going to get a lot better for the eventual online mode. And there will be an online mode, right? Even if Rockstar hasn't technically announced one is on the way yet.

On the flipside, if you're constantly getting griefed by a guy that only plays GTA 6 all day and won't let you leave your house in GTA Online, perhaps you could argue the game was better when it was single-player only.

It pains me to admit it, but GTA 6 is not only going to eventually run better on PC. It might be the definitive version in my eyes, but console gamers do have a high-fidelity future ahead of them, too. Both Sony and Microsoft are planning newly introduced consoles that seem pretty likely to come out in roughly a year's time—providing the memory crisis doesn't ruin everything—and AMD is set to be providing more powerful silicon for these systems.

It has been revealed that we're expecting to see the RDNA 5 architecture make its way into the next-gen consoles, paired with Zen 6 CPU cores of some size and description (these may be heterogeneous). That would put the consoles on a level playing field with PC components likely to launch around the same time (Zen 6 should be available on desktop by then, while perhaps a more limited launch for RDNA 5 by early 2028).

So that whole spiel about how current-gen consoles are years behind our fancy PCs won't get me so far once these latest systems come out. I'll have to find a new stick to bash consoles with… er, not enough RGB LEDs? Anyways, the definitive GTA 6 experience on console is still yet to come—that'll be the version that's ready to make the most of these more capable units sometime next year or in 2028.

There are going to be a helluva lot of patches, upgrades, and DLCs to come for GTA 6. Remember, GTA V got a latest first-person mode with the then-next-gen PS4 and Xbox One, so there's plenty of opportunity for genuine upgrades down the line.

Recent findings suggest that though, saying that, by recent PC standards (poor ports, game-breaking bugs, and more), this GTA 6 launch has been relatively problem-free. I mean, I've seen a couple of visual glitches and my colleagues have had some strange men falling out of the sky, but besides those open-world oddities you may expect of a game of this size and stature, it's been pretty smooth sailing so far.

It has been revealed that I just hope the PC version can claim a similarly clean sweep for its eventual launch. So far, no word on when that might be.

Available June 3 through July 29, the newly introduced event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

It has been revealed that along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

Industry observers note that the developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

Sources indicate that episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

It has been revealed that sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a fresh Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

On the eve of GTA 6 finally making its debut, it seems a lucky few have been given a special way to play it.

Several NBA players, all belonging to the Miami Heat team, have received a crazy care package from Rockstar Games that includes a special edition PS5 Pro console that's not publicly available.

Industry observers note that the console essentially matches the GTA 6 DualSense controllers, which are available to purchase. The machine sports the VI logo in one corner, has a black-on-black, embossed palm tree motif, and the blades across the console are that telltale neon pink and blue.

It looks great, and the package also comes with two of the matching controllers and a copy of GTA 6 itself. It's all delivered in a suitcase adorned in the same stylings.

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

Sources indicate that founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website claims the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it revealed a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched, and underperformance among significant releases. Ubisoft said in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Sources indicate that ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot remarked today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio.".

  • Industry observers note that in any case, the upgrade goes a tad further than that.

A major part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 enhancement next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

In a recent development, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Fresh Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

Industry observers note that in any case, the upgrade goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

In a recent development, overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something vital or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

That's a huge difference. Of course, the hours that it took for X-2 really paid off, as Alan Cumming (and Rebecca Romijn) looked incredible in that sequel. We'll just have to wait and see if fans change their mind when they get to see Nightcrawler in all his glory.

Industry observers note that I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what latest horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

It is time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5. Did we not say goodbye literally yesterday, when I installed a mod named Farewell Los Santos, and there was even a video and everything, and we put Komm Susser Tod over it?

Recent findings suggest that no. 53 mods ago, I told you, the reader, that my mission here was to either mod GTA 5 into a version of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PC, or break the game trying. Admittedly, my mission was successful: GTA 5 is actually better than GTA 6 now. But that means only one thing: as a final send-off, I can think of nothing better to do than finally fulfil the other potential outcome of our initial gambit. It is time to break GTA 5 entirely.

I have installed Fences Network, Simple Weapons Saving, Dragon Trainer V – How to Train Your Dragon Mega Pack, Empire: Singleplayer Overhaul, In The Hood (Gang), BodyGuard Menu, Addon Car Spawner Plus, Rideable Sandworm, Buckme Money App, Realistic Tactical Loadout - GTA VI Inspired Visible Weapon Carry, Pickup, & HUD System [Legacy & Enhanced], Gang Mod Respect System, Los Santos Collapse [Legacy & Enhanced] Zombie mod, The Last Heist - An ending for GTA V [Story Mod | 10 Missions], Real Life Mod [Legacy], Raul's Revenge DLC, Warzone Infil, RageHandlingEditor (RHE) [Legacy & Enhanced], On foot radio (with animations and headphones customization), Keep Right, and Ending C with M83 Midnight City.

In other words, everything that was on the front page of GTA 5 Mods dot com's scripts section when I loaded it up this morning. This took some doing, involving quite a lot of faffing around with OpenIV and myriad .rpf packages to get everything installed.

Would you be surprised to hear (you will not be surprised to hear) the game does not start anymore? GTA 5 has gone to that great sleep that awaits us all. Oh, don't get me wrong: it will boot to the main menu, but try to resume a game or start a newly introduced one and GTA 5 will, valiantly, spend about a minute and a half with its cogs audibly grinding against another before simply dumping you back at your desktop—no fanfare, no error message, just swift death. After enduring 53 other mods without completely breaking, it rests now in the great beyond.

I can't wait to do this to GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shang-Chi first debuted in 2021's Shang Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, but as was recently teased by Marvel, we haven't really heard from him since. The character is now set to return to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, where he'll team up in the fight against Doctor Doom.

It's not clear if his absence will be addressed in the upcoming superhero movie, but in a fresh interview, actor Simu Liu has shared his head canon about where his character has been this whole time, and it actually makes a lot of sense.

Appearing on the Countdown to Doomsday podcast, Liu was asked about what he thinks Shang-Chi has been up to. After some discussion about how he's definitely been fired from his job, Liu shared an insight into his character's backstory.

"I actually think that he's much more likely to go back to Ta Lo," he told the hosts, referencing the gorgeous mystical realm that his characters visits in his movie. "Just because he experiences for such a short period of time before stuff starts to go haywire. But it's really that peace of just remembering what it was like to drive through that for the first time, the experience of the animals but also to reconnect with his aunt and his family, I imagine that's probably really powerful for him.".

It has been revealed that liu went on to add that his return may also come "from a place of humility" as "he's just gotten these rings and he has no idea really how to use them." In Liu's mind, he got lucky in the movie's final fight, and ended up channeling the skills of his parents. "I think maybe there was some realization that he had to go and hone his powers still," he added.

Well, it looks like he's mastered them now from what we've seen in the Avengers: Doomsday trailers so far. He's set to face Gambit at some point too, which Liu compared to his iconic bus fight in Shang Chi and the Legend of the 10 Rings in an interview with Empire.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The initial reviews have arrived for GTA 6, and it's safe to say the game has been an absolute smash hit with critics.
  • Sources indicate that the metascore has settled on a 99, making it one point off a "perfect" score of 100.
  • More than that, though, it's the highest rated game of all time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The initial reviews have arrived for GTA 6, and it's safe to say the game has been an absolute smash hit with critics.

Sources indicate that the metascore has settled on a 99, making it one point off a "perfect" score of 100. In a year stuffed with fantastic games big and small, it's become the highest rated title of 2026.

More than that, though, it's the highest rated game of all time.

Reaching 99 is almost unheard of; only one other game has achieved the same level of acclaim — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998).

Recent findings suggest that however, GTA 6 has held onto its 99 score after more than 160 reviews; Ocarina of Time's metascore counts just 22 — though that's of course indicative of the era in which it released. There are simply more gaming outlets now, but that just means it's tougher to get consistent scores.

Rockstar's crime caper has received insanely consistent acclaim, and that might just give it an edge over the Nintendo classic. It's incredibly rare to see near-total agreement on a subjective work like this.

Critics are unanimous in their praise of GTA 6's open world, the relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia, and the complex systems behind its myriad characters, activities, and missions.

Here are some snippets from just a few of the reviews — including our own, of course.

According to recent reports, "GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a newly introduced sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.".

"Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.".

Industry observers note that "Like all videogame protagonists, Jason and Lucia are ciphers through which the player exerts their will on the digital world. And yet, through the co-authored interplay of the characters Rockstar has written, and the people you personally tune them into becoming, they form one of the great partnerships in entertainment: beautiful and deadly, open to the possibilities of their world and, despite the violence they inflict on those beyond their circle, driven forward not by fear, but by love.".

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content.".

Recent findings suggest that "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

"Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realising such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is a modern masterpiece. Rockstar's developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched. Minor performance issues don’t dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait.".

Sources indicate that earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

According to recent reports, what is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a significant upcoming lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an upgrade there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as massive a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

You'd better get used to seeing GTA 6 break records, because the game's not even out yet in most countries and it's already crushing long-standing numbers.

Indeed, the hype is so colossal that Rockstar's open worlder broke the all-time record for livestream viewers just minutes after its release in regions where it's already the 19th November.

According to Streams Charts' data, GTA 6 has peaked a frankly absurd 7.2 million viewers across streaming platforms Twitch (3.1 million), YouTube (2.7 million), and Kick (1.4 million), and others.

The crazy part is that this figure could well be eclipsed as GTA 6 becomes available in more regions, and more streamers start to broadcast their gameplay.

Team-based shooter Valorant previously held the all-time record, which was set back in 2020, when watching livestreams could net you access to the game's PC beta.

It peaked at 1.7 million viewers, meaning that GTA 6 has absolutely demolished the record — and honestly, it's hard to imagine anything topping it for years and years to come.

Recent findings suggest that have you contributed to any of these numbers by watching someone else play GTA 6? Or are you saving the experience for your own playthrough? Try not to spoil yourself in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've accepted that Arnold Schwarzenegger can probably do things at 79 that would put me in physical therapy. Still, watching him take time from his busy 2026 movie schedule to hoist an enormous Christmas tree overhead while dressed as Santa Claus made me do a double take. The moment comes from a newly introduced Santa Schwarzenegger holiday ad, which follows the action icon through New York City in a Santa suit as he dodges the paparazzi. Somehow, he winds up helping a family load a tree onto their car. I suspect some movie magic made that lift possible, but seeing Arnold casually handle an entire evergreen is pretty funny. It also has me wondering: What's it like doing stunts at his age?

The Santa clip landed on Arnold's Instagram just days after the former governor got candid about what action scenes feel like at his age. During his November 11 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Schwarzenegger discussed the possibility of returning to Predator, Commando, and Conan the Barbarian. Kimmel brought up King Conan, which would follow his famous warrior as an older ruler whose reign is threatened. When the conversation turned to the demands of filming that kind of movie, Arnold admitted the years have made a difference:.

I tell you one thing, to do all this action and the sword fighting and horseback riding, and all this stuff is not as easy anymore today than it was 40 years ago…. Well, you get older and you slow down a little bit, right?

Sources indicate that four decades ago, Schwarzenegger swung swords and ran through jungles. I'd imagine climbing onto a horse in full costume feels a little different at 79. Of course, he wasn't about to let a serious observation about aging ruin a perfectly good joke. He rapidly followed up with a line that had me laughing:.

No, not very much. But still, I'm now at an age where it takes me an hour and a half to watch 60 Minutes. Unbelievable, I think. Things are really slowing down.

According to recent reports, that's a pretty fantastic old-man joke. The timing is even better when you remember this is the same guy presently showing up in Amazon’s holiday commercial looking capable of bench-pressing a Christmas tree. Kimmel also commented on how muscular Schwarzenegger still is, which led to some playful back-and-forth between the two. Even the Terminator is still perfectly comfortable being the butt of his own jokes.

A post shared by Arnold Schwarzenegger (@schwarzenegger).

According to recent reports, schwarzenegger isn't pretending he can simply pick up where he left off in 1986, either. He's spoken about how a potential King Conan would acknowledge the character's age, with Conan having spent decades on the throne before facing a threat to his kingdom. That's an idea I can get behind. CinemaBlend has already covered his updates about possible Predator and Commando sequels, although he told Kimmel he was still waiting to see finalized scripts.

Meanwhile, the Christmas tree is a nice bit of promotion for The Man with the Bag, Schwarzenegger's new Prime Video holiday movie with Reacher star Alan Ritchson and Awkwafina. In it, he plays Santa, who recruits a thief to recover his stolen bag of presents. The film arrives December 2 for anyone with a Prime Video subscription, marking his return to Christmas comedy 30 years after Jingle All the Way.

As for that tree lift, I'd love to see some behind-the-scenes footage before giving Arnold full credit for the feat. But the man seems to be having a blast playing Santa, and I hope he keeps finding excuses to do action scenes. Maybe someone can make him a really comfortable saddle for King Conan.

Industry observers note that amazon is offering early Black Friday discounts on like-fresh versions of its 2024 Kindles, with prices starting at $152.99 for the Paperwhite and savings of $27 to $75 across five models that include the color-screen Colorsoft and the pen-equipped Kindle Scribe. All five are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The company introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon has tested and certified to look and work like new.

The Like-Upcoming Kindle Paperwhite (16GB) is down to $152.99 from $179.99 and covers just about everything most people need for everyday reading, including enough storage for thousands of ebooks. Its seven-inch, 300ppi glare-free display is larger than the previous generation’s 6.8-inch screen, with faster page turns, an adjustable warm light, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life. As PCMag notes in its review, it's a great option for readers who don't need color or handwriting features.

The Like-Latest Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $190.99 from $224.99, making it just $38 more than the like-new Paperwhite (16GB). For that relatively small difference, you're doubling the storage to 32GB and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

Industry observers note that the Like-Latest Kindle Colorsoft (16GB) is down to $220.99 from $260.99 and offers something the Paperwhite models can’t: a color E-Ink display, which makes it well suited to comics, graphic novels, illustrated books, and travel guides. Its seven-inch screen reveals that color content at 150ppi while keeping text at a sharp 300ppi, and you can mark passages in multiple highlight colors to keep your notes organized. That said, colors are noticeably more muted than on a conventional tablet, and battery life tops out at eight weeks, compared with 12 weeks on the Paperwhite.

Recent findings suggest that the Like-Latest Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $243.99 from $287.99, making it just $23 more than the standard like-new Colorsoft. For that modest increase, you're getting twice the storage at 32GB, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

Sources indicate that the Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $284.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA games are substantial, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.
  • Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats.
  • Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are substantial, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats. But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:.

Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

GTA 6 is a significant, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Recent findings suggest that using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90 hours I found exactly one of them. Spawning a jet means first completing every single challenge in the game, which is gonna take, ooh, let me check… forever.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't love this cheat unlock system at all, but there's even more bad news:.

Industry observers note that want to use a cheat to give yourself an extra $250,000 so you can go on a car buying spree? Cool, go ahead. But you won't be able to save your progress once you enable a cheat.

Whatever fun you have cheating is purely of the sandbox variety. You can buy cars and clothes and guns with cheated money, but you'll lose it all when you stop playing because you're not allowed to save your game once you use a single cheat. Booo.

And there's one final bummer for ya:.

I tried it. I opened an older save where I hadn't yet completed the main story, and tried to input the cheats I'd learned from my complete game save. No dice! The cheats don't work unless you're using a save file that's story complete. So, starting over at the beginning and using cheats? Not gonna happen.

Industry observers note that I'm really not a fan of this. With so many restrictions in place, Rockstar has really taken the fun out of being a huge GTA cheater! When GTA 6 finally comes to PC, I hope modders make cheats their top priority.

Sources indicate that when you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a upcoming interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

Sources indicate that "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a newly introduced interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

Guide: GTA 6: Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1441 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know.
  • Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.
  • GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know. This spoiler-free GTA 6 guide includes info on a dozen key features and mechanics that will help you make the best start to your life in Vice City.

Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.

GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.

Press Options and select Settings > Gameplay. Scroll to the bottom (options 24 and 25) and you can choose to enable Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, as shown:.

Accessible Combat will both reduce the damage you take in gunfights, while increasing the damage enemies receive, making firefights much more manageable.

Recent findings suggest that reduced Vehicle Damage, meanwhile, will reduce the damage your car takes when in crashes or combat. This means there's less chance of your car becoming difficult to control or exploding.

The game will warn you that enabling these "changes the balance and experience of gameplay", meaning your experience will be a lot easier. Using them does not alter the story or disable Trophies, however.

GTA 6 has a fresh control scheme which modernises its gameplay by mapping run to L3 and jump to Cross/X.

For those of you who've spent over a decade playing GTA 5 and GTA Online, however, you may prefer to use Rockstar's more traditional control scheme.

Fortunately, this is relatively easy to enable.

Press Options and select Settings > Control Scheme, as pictured:.

The control scheme will automatically be set to the new Default layout, but you can toggle to Classic if you prefer the GTA 5 approach.

As its name implies, GTA 6 is all about grand theft auto — or, in other words, stealing cars.

Most vehicles you find parked around Vice City will be locked, but it is possible to steal them quicker with a very simple tip.

When the minigame for any criminal activities appear — like using your Slim Jim, Clone Key, or even hotwiring a car — there's a pink "sweet spot" you can find to speed up the action:.

This makes it quicker to break in and make a quick getaway.

Just move the sticks around to find the right spot, and use those extra seconds wisely to escape swiftly:.

GTA 6 has a living, breathing open world that encourages exploration. If you take the time to look around, you'll almost certainly discover something to do.

However, if you want to continue with the story and you're not sure what to do next, there's a way to easily see your next objective or story mission.

Press the Touch Pad to open your map and then using the index on the left of the screen, press Right to see a list of available story missions, with mandatory objectives at the top and optional ones listed below:.

You can immediately set a waypoint to any mission with Cross/X.

There is no traditional fast travel in GTA 6, but there is a way you can get around the map promptly for a nominal fee.

Bring up your smartphone by pressing Up and select RydeMe:.

You'll need to have an active waypoint, which you can choose from within the app or by picking one in advance via your map with Touch Pad.

You'll be notified a driver is on the way and you'll be able to see them from your minimap:.

Recent findings suggest that once you get in your Ryde, hold L2 to focus on your driver. You can then hold Triangle to skip your journey for $100 and immediately arrive at your destination:.

Longer journeys will cost more than shorter ones, but fast travelling this way is relatively inexpensive overall.

There are two types of money in GTA 6: cash stored in your wallet and money protected in your BuckMe bank. The latter will unlock as part of Chapter 1.

You can see both types of money at any time by pushing Down:.

Money stored in your wallet will be lost if you're Busted or Wasted during gameplay, so it's really vital you put this in your BuckMe bank.

The easiest way to do this is press Up to access your smartphone and select BuckMe > ATM Finder:.

It has been revealed that this will automatically select a waypoint to the nearest ATM machine. Follow it and deposit any funds in your wallet into your BuckMe bank, where it'll be safe even if you get arrested or die:.

Throughout GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will build a criminal profile which can affect how NPCs and the wider world of Leonida responds to you.

Recent findings suggest that murdering enemies will contribute towards a more aggressive criminal profile. As such, you may want to consider a non-lethal approach.

One way to do this is by favouring stealth and grabbing enemies with R2, so you can cleanly knock them out without killing them:.

Another option, if you get caught up in a gunfight, is to target non-vitals like kneecaps and arms.

You can easily see non-vitals by pressing L3 and R3 and aiming at yellow parts of the body:.

You'll know an enemy has been debilitated without killing them if a yellow X appears in your weapon's reticule. A red X will appear if your target has been murdered.

If you need to set a quick waypoint to an notable location in GTA 6, you don't necessarily need to press Touch Pad to bring up your map.

Instead, hold Down and you'll get an alternative in-game view of any nearby shops, waypoints, or story missions:.

You can highlight any of these and press R3 to automatically set a GPS route to where you want to go.

There'll be times in GTA 6 when you're separated from your car and you want to spawn it nearby.

You can do this by opening your smartphone with Up and selecting the Scooter Bros app:.

Select which car you want to use from the app and you'll be charged a fee depending on the delivery distance and your car's current condition:.

Your car will then automatically spawn in a nearby location, marked on your minimap:.

Stealing or entering a car in GTA 6 does not mean you'll have access to it forever.

You'll need to park it in a Parking Space or Garage to temporarily store it, and register it at a Pay 'N' Spray to keep it forever.

Find a car you want to keep and set a waypoint for a Pay 'N' Spray, like with this Emperor Sultan I just stole:.

Drive into the Pay 'N' Spray and select Register to swap the plates. The fee commanded will depend on the value of the car:.

Note that you will need free Stored Vehicle slots to register your car. You can sell previous cars directly at the Pay 'N' Spray:.

Industry observers note that alternatively, you can press Up to open your smartphone and select Vice City Real Estate. This will let you buy more garages for additional Parking Spots:.

This feature becomes available during a story mission, so you may not immediately have access to it if you're still early in the campaign.

Generic upgrades are available for all vehicles at any Mod Shop, but if you want specialist tunings you need to go to the right shop.

These are marked with a blue Wrench icon.

Press Up to open your map and then Right to open the map index.

Select Vehicles > Mod Shops and look for a Mod Shop with a blue Wrench icon, as shown:.

Set a waypoint for the appropriate Mod Shop and you'll find all of the customisations and specialised upgrades available for your current vehicle.

Just like in real-life, staying on top of your smartphone notifications in GTA 6 can be time consuming.

Fortunately, the game will mark important messages for you in the Reminders tab:.

Press Up to bring up your smartphone and then press Square to access your Reminders.

Here you'll find a curated list of key messages, including in-game news articles and NPCs who are waiting for your replies:.

Recent findings suggest that hopefully you've learned a thing or two with this spoiler-free GTA 6 walkthrough and collectibles guide. Are there any other tips and tricks you think the world should know? Share them in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that "The fun thing about watching a film in the home is a different kind of concentration," Nolan told Polygon.
  • According to recent reports, as Nolan explains, at home, you can zero in on different elements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IMAX might be the best way to watch Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, but the director has shared the bright side of watching his Greek mythology epic at home, too.

Recent findings suggest that "The fun thing about watching a film in the home is a different kind of concentration," Nolan told Polygon. "When you go to a movie, you're in the dark, you're really focused for a couple hours. In the home, it's a different type of concentration because you can pause the movie, you can go get a snack, come back.".

According to recent reports, as Nolan explains, at home, you can zero in on different elements. "It does allow you to control the timeline and really look at the detail of things," he added. "And for me, it's really about the performances.".

Recent findings suggest that plus, the director encourages watching more than once. "The human element is what connects you with the story," he noted. "But I think the work of these actors, this cast, this incredible cast in the film, it rewards multiple viewings.".

The Odyssey's absolutely massive ensemble cast includes the likes of the fresh James Bond, Robert Pattinson, as well as Tom Holland, Matt Damon, Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway, Jon Bernthal, and many more.

"There's subtleties and nuances in what they're doing that I, in the edit suite, get to watch again and again and again and sort of pick up on all the different things that Matt or Anne or Tom or Rob, what they're bringing to things, or Samantha Morton," Nolan continued. "It's really fun for people to be able to look at that in the home and see all the different layers that these guys have put into the story.".

According to recent reports, while you can watch the film at home, however, don't expect to see any deleted scenes. "There's a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan shared recently. "I don't really believe in director's cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren't many scenes that were shot.".

Sources indicate that the Odyssey is returning to IMAX 70mm this December if you missed it the first time around. With a current box office total of over $1.8 billion, it's the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever.

For more, check out our The Odyssey review, or our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that to say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

Sources indicate that the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being noted, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just introduced into early access.

Industry observers note that to say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be substantial or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.
